item.title: Gambonanza Early Board Money Guide - How to Farm Stock Fast on a 5x5 Opening Board
item.description:
The Opening Board Is Your Real Money Engine

The Short Version

Every Gambonanza run starts on a 5x5 board with 3 pieces, and every board growth step only happens after you beat a boss checkpoint. That means the first several games of any run are played on a small, cramped board, and that cramped board is also where your economy is most fragile. Farming Stock here is not about a secret opener. It is about understanding that you earn money for winning games, and then spending that money correctly in the shop. The Economy Guide covers the full investment picture, and the Board Size Strategy Guide explains why small boards change your build.

item.title: Why Your Gambit Did Not Fire? Real Tile Interactions and How to Read Them
item.description:
You placed your Gambit piece on what looked like a perfectly normal tile. The activation animation did not play. The Gambit did not trigger. Your gold is gone, and you are staring at a silent board wondering what went wrong.

There is no hidden “dark tile” or “ghost tile” rule in Gambonanza. What actually happens is simpler and more predictable: specific tiles have specific effects, and some of those effects change what a Gambit can do when a piece stands on them. Once you know the real tile list, you stop guessing.

item.title: Crumble Mode Changes in Gambonanza 1.4: Stasis Waiting Is Safe Now
item.description:
Crumble Mode is the pressure system in Gambonanza that punishes passive play: every turn you stall without making progress nudges the crumble counter toward a board-wide wipe. In v1.4.0, one balance change quietly rewrites how you survive a bad board. Waiting against a Stasis enemy no longer increases the Crumble Mode counter.

That single line is enormous for anyone who stalls on purpose. Before 1.4, sitting still on a Stasis-controlled lane was a slow death sentence: the longer you waited, the closer you drifted toward a forced crumble. After 1.4, you can hold a Stasis lane indefinitely without feeding the counter. Stasis zones become safe pockets where you can wait out bad boards, scout incoming enemy formations, or line up a promotion without the clock punishing you.

item.title: Gambonanza Custom Boards Guide - How to Unlock All 21 Boards (17 Unlockable)
item.description:
Added in v1.2.0, Board Customization lets you choose from 21 different boards (4 default + 17 unlockable). Each board is purely cosmetic. No gameplay advantage. But the unlock conditions range from trivial to genuinely challenging. This guide covers every board, how to unlock it, and the fastest unlock path.

Board customization unlocks in the main menu after your first win. Access it from the “Customize” tab.

item.title: Board Full of Pieces? The Pruning Priority Guide - What to Sell First When Space Runs Out
item.description: Your board is full, a new Gambit piece just spawned, and you have 3 seconds to decide what to sell. From my own runs across every stage, I found that indecision costs more gold than bad decisions. Players who freeze and overthink lose 2 to 3 turns of tempo. This guide gives you a priority system that eliminates the thinking entirely. The Piece Sacrifice Guide covers this in depth. The Economy Guide covers this in depth.

item.title: Gambonanza Crumble Mode Guide - The Timer That Shrinks the Board
item.description:
Crumble pacing changed in v1.4.0. With Enhanced AI Mode on, the AI avoids crumbling tiles more carefully and Crumble triggers later, so you get a bit more room early. See the Crumble Mode changes guide.

Gambonanza is a game with two clocks. One is the board itself: tiles fall away as a game runs, taking any piece standing on them. The other is the Stalemate Counter, which ends a game outright if neither side moves the position forward. Together they make sure no game lasts forever.

item.title: Gambonanza Gold Tile Guide - Getting Paid to Land
item.description:
Gold Tiles, Explained

Gold Tiles pay out when you land a piece on them. There is no spectral piece system and no ghost piece to convert, so treat this page as the real answer: Gold Tiles are a way to get paid for a landing you were going to make anyway.

THE SHORT VERSION

Landing from Stock costs a full turn. A Gold Tile turns that turn into a payout. The skill is timing: land on gold when you needed to land, not just because the tile is shiny.

item.title: Gambonanza Board Growth Guide - How the Board Expands Through a Run
item.description:
Gambonanza Board Growth Guide - How the Board Expands Through a Run

Quick Fix

You do not choose your board size, and you do not play on 8x8 boards. A run starts on a 5x5 board and grows by a row after every stage you clear. Playing the opening board like a huge late-game board is the fastest way to lose tempo.

Stage of the run Board What changes
Stage 1 5x5 Cramped, every square matters, knights dominate
Mid stages 6x5, 7x5 More room, longer threats, files start to open
Late stages Larger Real space, set up bigger traps and longer plans

The golden rule: the smaller the board, the more every single square and every single move matters. As the board grows, your plans get longer and safer. Adapt to the board you are on, not the one you wish you had.

item.title: Tile Control Guide
item.description:
Tile Control TL;DR Check Crumble Mechanic Guide for the full breakdown. The Decision Framework breaks this down in detail.

Center = wins. Edges = Crumble bait.

Gambonanza is territory control, not chess. Control the center tiles and the game plays itself.

AOnce you see the board as territory, everything else makes sense.

Tile Value Map (5x5)

Tier Value Crumble Safety Best Piece
S (center) Highest Never collapses Queen / Knight
A (mid-ring) High Collapses last Rook / Bishop
B (bridge) Medium Collapses mid-game Any
C (corridor) Low Collapses early Avoid
D (edge) Lowest 1st to collapse Avoid

Gambit Tiles Quick Reference

Tile Effect Priority
Blessed Tile Captured blessed piece returns to Stock ?(excellent)
Gold Tile Piece turns to gold and gains money value ?(always take)
Protective Tile Protects a piece for 1 turn ?(take vs boss)
Trap Tile Enemy that steps on it cannot move next turn ?(drop on lanes)
Cursed Tile Boss-placed, downgrades your piece to a pawn ?(avoid)

Rule: Gold and Blessed Tiles are the most valuable on the board. Plan routes to land your pieces on them.
